top.headline: Democrat Scott Colom Leads Mississippi's Senate Race by Fewer Than 100 Votes
top.blurb: Democrat Scott Colom leads Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by fewer than 100 votes in Mississippi's Senate race, with more than 95% of ballots counted and roughly 15,000 provisional ballots still outstanding. A win would make him the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction; Mississippi has no automatic recount law, and results must be certified by November 13.

top.headline: Virginia Voters Repeal a 124-Year-Old Lifetime Voting Ban Written to Disenfranchise Black Residents
top.blurb: Virginians voted by more than 10 points to restore voting rights immediately upon release from a felony sentence, repealing an 1902 constitutional provision that 100 white male delegates wrote explicitly to disenfranchise Black voters. More than 250,000 Virginians were affected; only Iowa and Kentucky still impose a comparable lifetime ban.

top.headline: Democrats Prepare to Investigate DHS as They Take Control of Congress
top.blurb: Senator Maggie Hassan, incoming chair of the Senate Homeland Security Committee, is hiring an anti-corruption counsel and oversight investigators, while House Democrats have demanded DHS preserve records ahead of promised inquiries into Kristi Noem, Corey Lewandowski and other officials. Lewandowski is already under criminal investigation over allegations he profited from his government role.

top.headline: Kerala Orders Probe Into Fresh Bribery Allegations Against Election Commission Chief Gyanesh Kumar
top.blurb: Kerala has ordered a preliminary probe after a contractor alleged Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar sought a Rs 2 crore bribe and withheld Rs 17 crore in approved bills as a state PWD official in 2006, tied to the suicide of a project engineer that year. The claim lands amid nationwide protests demanding Kumar's resignation over the voter-roll revision.

top.headline: Delhi Government Clears Contempt Case Against Activist Who Accused a Judge of 'Serving the Master'
top.blurb: Delhi's government approved contempt proceedings against Cockroach Janta Party legal head Ratna Singh over posts accusing a Saket court judge of 'serving the master,' after he rejected her plea over her October detention at a protest demanding the Election Commission chief's resignation. The government says her claim that an unnamed 'master' was directing the judge and police went unsupported.

top.headline: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay Asks Modi to Finally Give the Supreme Court a Permanent Chennai Bench
top.blurb: Chief Minister Vijay revived a demand Tamil Nadu has pursued since 1980, arguing that travelling to Delhi puts the Supreme Court's remedies out of reach for litigants across the south. The Court's Full Bench rejected the idea in 2007 despite Tamil Nadu's offer of infrastructure, and the government told Parliament in 2024 it saw no need to revisit that position.

top.headline: Death Toll From Russian Strike on Ukrainian Aid Centre Rises to 40
top.blurb: Zelenskyy raised the death toll from Tuesday's strikes on a school-turned-aid-centre in Komyshuvakha to 40, with more than 30 people still feared under the rubble, and called it a 'vile terrorist' attack. The UN's human rights mission in Ukraine said the bombing likely broke international law; Russian and Ukrainian delegations are now due in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11.

top.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Claims Tanker Fires and Captured US Drones in the Strait of Hormuz
top.blurb: Iran's IRGC said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after attempting an 'unauthorised route,' and claimed its electronic warfare units captured two US drones intact. Supreme Leader Khamenei said the US midterm results change nothing and that American hostility toward Iran will continue regardless.

top.headline: South Korea Moves to Extend Its Anti-Piracy Patrol Toward the Strait of Hormuz
top.blurb: Seoul plans to roughly double the range of its Cheonghae anti-piracy unit, pushing it toward Oman's coast under pressure from Trump to help secure shipping near Hormuz, while insisting the noncombat mission stays under Korean command. Opposition lawmakers call it a disguised deployment that could expose troops to Iranian retaliation.

top.headline: India Chase Down New Zealand in a Rain-Hit Series Opener as Kohli Hits 74
top.blurb: India beat New Zealand by five wickets on the DLS method at Eden Park, Auckland, to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match ODI series. Virat Kohli top-scored with 74 off 51 balls in the rain-curtailed chase, while Anshul Kamboj took Player of the Match honours with 2 for 22.

more.headline: Starc Reclaims Test Bowling's No. 1 Spot After a Nine-Wicket Haul in Cape Town
more.blurb: Mitchell Starc overtook South Africa's Marco Jansen for the top Test bowling ranking after a nine-wicket match haul, while Simon Harmer jumped nine places and Shreyas Iyer rose to seventh among T20I batters after India's series win in New Zealand.

top.headline: 'Ramayana: Part 1' Review: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash Anchor a Sleek, Overstuffed Spectacle
top.blurb: Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic opens with Raavan's rise before following Ram's exile and Sita's abduction. Critic Nandini Ramnath calls it a sleek, Hollywood-style spectacle anchored by Yash's gangster-inflected Raavan, but finds the reverent dialogue stiff and the 195-minute runtime overstuffed; Part 2 arrives in 2028.

bengal.headline: Jhargram to Get a Tiger Safari, With Five Royal Bengals Expected From Siliguri
bengal.blurb: West Bengal plans a 65-acre tiger safari at Jhargram's Jangalmahal zoo, with five surplus tigers due from Siliguri and completion expected within two years, following the Siliguri safari model.

bengal.headline: Suvendu Adhikari Reiterates Target of 1 Lakh Government Job Appointments by May 2027
bengal.blurb: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari restated his pledge of 1 lakh appointment letters by May 2027 while announcing roughly 8,200 new Panchayat recruitment posts, promising the process would be merit-based.

travel.headline: Mexico's Pan de Muerto Blends Aztec Offerings and Catholic Ritual Into One Sweet Bread
travel.blurb: The orange-scented, bone-topped bread eaten during Dia de los Muertos traces to 18th-century bakers blending Spanish graveside offerings with Indigenous Mesoamerican traditions of feeding the dead.

travel.headline: Six Million Antelope Trace 'Lines of Life' Across South Sudan in the Planet's Largest Mammal Migration
travel.blurb: GPS collars on 262 animals since 2023 mapped the routes of roughly six million kob, tiang, gazelle and reedbuck across South Sudan's Great Nile Migration Landscape, where commercial hunting and new roads increasingly threaten their corridors.

happy.headline: 'No One You Love Is Ever Dead': Hemingway's Letter on Grief and the Meaning of Life
happy.blurb: After the death of their young son Baoth, Ernest Hemingway wrote to his grieving friends Gerald and Sara Murphy with a line that has comforted mourners ever since: that no one truly loved is ever gone.

tech_top.headline: Anthropic Pays a Publisher for the First Time, Licensing AP Content for Election Night
tech_top.pm_note: Anthropic had insisted its use of publisher content was fair use just months ago — watch how fast a 'no licensing deals' policy flips once a product gap, here live election data, makes the cost of not paying obvious.
tech_top.blurb: Anthropic quietly struck its first paid content deal with a digital publisher, giving Claude real-time, AP-attributed election results on Tuesday night after premium outlets' blocking of AI crawlers left it weak on breaking news. OpenAI already has more than a dozen such licensing deals; Anthropic calls this one a limited experiment ahead of its expected IPO.

tech_top.headline: Democrats' Midterm Sweep Could Slow the US Data Center Boom, Analysts Say
tech_top.pm_note: 38 ballot measures restricting data centers passed in one week — treat local permitting and community opposition as a first-class line item in any infrastructure-dependent roadmap, not a footnote.
tech_top.blurb: Voters approved 38 ballot measures restricting data centers as Democrats also won governors' races in Texas and Georgia on promises to pause construction, potentially stalling some 13 gigawatts of planned Texas capacity alone. Semiconductor and hardware stocks fell on the news, though economists expect delay rather than derailment of the broader AI buildout.

tech_more.headline: AI-Generated 'Vibe-Coded' Addons Are Already Flooding World of Warcraft: Forever
tech_more.blurb: Ahead of the relaunch's debut, Warcraft Logs says AI-generated addons copying established developers' work have grown from a handful of abusers to roughly 1 in 10 API users, prompting the site to add a paid commercial tier.

tech_101.text: An agreement where an AI company pays a publisher for the right to use its articles or data, rather than relying on 'fair use' or scraping the open web — increasingly how AI firms get access to the paywalled, credible reporting their chatbots need for breaking news.

Short for capital expenditure — the billions tech companies spend building data centers and buying chips to train and run AI. It's the number investors watch most closely, and the one local ballot measures and permitting fights are now starting to slow.

science.headline: Scientists Use Cancer Cells' Own Chemistry to Manufacture the Drug That Kills Them
science.blurb: RIKEN chemists built an albumin-wrapped palladium catalyst that reacts with the unusually high carbon monoxide levels inside tumor cells to synthesize a toxic anticancer compound there and nowhere else. In lab tests on liver, cervical, breast and lung cancer cells, the drug formed only inside the cancer cells, sparing a noncancerous line and blood; animal studies are next.

science.headline: NASA Weighs a Commercial Rescue to Keep Hubble From Falling Out of the Sky
science.blurb: More than 35 years into its mission, Hubble has no propulsion to fight the atmospheric drag pulling it toward a reentry NASA now estimates for 2033 or 2034. The agency has asked private companies to propose a boost, a servicing mission, or a safe disposal, with a launch needed by 2032 to avoid reentry.

science.headline: Physicists Confirm a Third Type of Magnetism Nearly a Century After the First Two
science.blurb: SLAC researchers used circularly polarized X-rays to show that manganese telluride responds differently to left- and right-handed light — the signature of 'altermagnetism,' a state with zero net magnetization but spin-polarized currents that could make for faster, more stable computer memory.

philosophy.headline: Gut Feelings Aren't Just Noise — They Work the Same Way as Careful Reasoning
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Marc Moffett argues that everyday intuitions — sensing a stranger is off, an email is a scam — are rationally justified, not mere shortcuts, resting on the same 'presentational' cognitive posture philosophers have long reserved for logic and thought experiments. Gut feelings, he writes, deserve neither blind trust nor dismissal.

philosophy.headline: In Praise of the Dilettante: Why Refusing to Specialise Is a Way of Life Worth Defending
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Jay Miller defends the dilettante against centuries of scorn from Goethe to today's productivity culture, arguing that moving freely between pursuits — neither dabbler nor passive flaneur — offers a legitimate abundance rather than a lack of seriousness, drawing on Kierkegaard's aesthete and Nietzsche's free spirit.

philosophy_101.text: The idea that chains of justification for our beliefs can't go on forever — at some point, justification has to come from something that isn't itself a belief, like a perceptual experience or an intuition, which can justify without needing justification of its own.

A classic philosophical distinction: negative freedom is freedom FROM constraints, like rules or gatekeeping, while positive freedom is the freedom TO actively pursue and explore. The 'dilettante' as a way of life leans on both — escaping a profession's rules while still choosing to go deep.
